meta.title: Reyes's night

moments.what: Night, 00:30:00 station clock. Reyes asleep in Quarters 2. No alarm. Her evidence card points to: room (quarters-2)
The air stops moving in Quarters 2: the room plays the climb in NASA's record
Room alarm: Quarters 2's 1-hour CO2 average is 3 mmHg, 0.01 over NASA's 3 mmHg limit
reyes: level 2 raised, room-limit in quarters-2 (0.01 mmHg over), told to reyes and okafor, "Are you OK?" countdown 60 s
reyes: level 3 escalated, room-limit in quarters-2 (0.01 mmHg over), told to everyone, steps card high-co2, message to Earth arrives 02:09:20, reply 02:29:20
The board in galley sounds its buzzer
Okafor taps "I've seen it" on Reyes's level 3 and heads to Quarters 2
The board in galley goes quiet
Okafor, the Crew Medical Officer, reaches Quarters 2
okafor: level 2 raised, room-limit in quarters-2 (0.02 mmHg over), told to okafor, "You entered a room over the limit" countdown 300 s
Okafor gets Reyes out to the galley
Airflow restored: the room plays a calm stretch of NASA's record
Room alarm clears: Quarters 2's 1-hour CO2 average is back to 3 mmHg
At the end: message to Earth about reyes (sent 01:49:20) still listed, alert ended 01:52:50, reply can arrive 02:29:20, still pending

record.files: data-nasa/osdr-rr1/co2.json, temperature-iss.json, humidity-iss.json (NASA OSDR, ISS, RR-1, 20 Sep to 1 Nov 2014)
record.conversion: CO2 in mmHg = co2_iss (read as ppm) x 760 / 1,000,000, rounded to 2 decimals
record.rule: A row at scenario time t in a room plays that room's record time recordFrom + (t - from), on the record's 5-minute grid counted from its first row (2014-09-20T03:59Z): the grid slot at or before that time. The record's own timestamps drift up to 2 minutes from that grid (the sample stamped 22:43 sits in the 22:44 slot); a slot with no sample repeats the one before (11 of 12,096).

notes: Simulated scenario. The crew, their bodies, where they are and where they move are simulated.
Every room's CO2, temperature and humidity are NASA's ISS record, replayed unchanged: real values, another place and date.

Quarters 2 plays three stretches of the record: the one the live demo plays, then the climb from 2014-10-21T22:44:00Z, then a calm stretch from 2014-10-15T00:39:00Z. The climb past 3 mmHg is the record's own. The recovery is a jump to a calm stretch, because nothing in the record falls fast from above 3 mmHg.
The room alarm judges the 1-hour average of the replayed rows stored in the room, so for the first hour of the climb it mixes the stretch before the air stopped with the climb.
Reyes's body readings are the ordinary simulated ones; nothing in the scenario changes them.
Pressure, oxygen, noise, light, vibration, air quality and radiation are the hub's simulated stand-in values.

Thinned for size: each signal of each room and person is kept at most once every 30 seconds of the scenario's clock (a screen counts a reading as current for that long), and a replayed value also whenever it changes. The hub made 47256 rows during the night; this file keeps 15036. Every other message is kept as sent.
